deposits.notes: Public preregistration #163203, CreAItive Collaboration, registered 2024/02/22 02:32 (PT), with the same authors and design as S1. The cited .pdf URL now serves an HTML registration page (HTTP 200). Its Download PDF link returned HTTP 200, application/pdf, filename AsPredicted #163203.pdf, 200480 bytes, 2 pages; the PDF was read entirely in memory. Its explicitly linked archive mirror, https://archive.org/download/aspredicted/msym-tbc2.pdf, also returned HTTP 200, application/pdf, 200480 bytes. The mirror is the same registration and is not counted as a separate deposit. The registration describes the two planned conditions, AUT scoring, intended semantic-distance analysis, exclusions, and intended sample size. It contains no observed participant-to-arm assignments, realized scores, participant texts, or data/code files. Planned conditions do not count as has_arm_assignment. Generic ResearchBox navigation is not a link to a study-specific deposit. No data-use license was stated.

The paper repeatedly refers to Supplementary Materials but gives no supplementary-file URL or filename. The publisher landing page returned HTTP 403 with a Cloudflare Just a moment challenge; stopped without attempting to bypass it. The supplementary file list and contents could not be inspected. This is a potential supplementary-material location, not a confirmed dataset. The paper describes consent documentation, task-interface screenshots/descriptions, questionnaires, AUT scoring details, sample descriptive statistics/bias analyses, and two example human-AI interactions. Those descriptions do not establish availability of the full participant/dyad-level data. The empty files array means unlisted, not zero files. A bot check does not establish that an account or access request is required, hence access=unclear rather than restricted/account_required. The main paper is CC BY 4.0 (p. 1), but that does not confirm a separate supplementary-data license.

notes: Checked 2026-10-09 using Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1, without authentication or personal identifiers. Read all 105829 characters of the markdown conversion in seven contiguous chunks, including the complete references; the 17-page paper has no appended supplement or embedded files. All recorded sharing/preregistration statements were checked against PDF text; quotes normalize line-break whitespace only. No formal data/code availability statement, on-request offer, or dataset repository URL was found. The form data_and_code fields are empty. Public material confirmed for the randomized S1 study is the preregistration; no participant/dyad/output-level dataset with observed arm assignments and outcomes was located. Thus code_or_materials_only refers to the public registration, not to a verified public copy of the ACM supplementary materials. Public data do not currently permit calculation of missing arm-specific AUT means, SDs/SEs, analyzed retention counts/attrition, dyad-level elaboration tests or the Figure 14 correlation, randomized/excluded flow counts, or text/idea diversity. Coder reliability and interim AI-use results also remain unresolved. The missing ACM supplement could contain additional information, so failure to find a dataset is not proof that none exists. Related publication check, not counted as a data deposit: reference [7] on p. 15 links to https://chi-trew.github.io/papers/2024/CHI_TREW_2024_Paper_6.pdf . It returned HTTP 200, application/pdf, 737996 bytes, 8 pages. The referenced GitHub hosting repository was listed once through https://api.github.com/repos/chi-trew/chi-trew.github.io/git/trees/HEAD?recursive=1 (HTTP 200, truncated=false, 136 files, tree SHA 77b6f44273b30746b7ad3e56588604c1453e56b4). The listed files are workshop PDFs and website assets, with no identifiable study dataset or analysis-code deposit; papers/2024/CHI_TREW_2024_Paper_6.pdf is the matching publication. This paper concerns the nonrandomized S2 pre-study and provides published aggregate results, not the S1 randomized data. No study-data availability/deposit statement or embedded data file was found in it. It can assist a later primary-source audit of S2: p. 3, Section 4.3 directly states 40 human participants, mostly psychology students from an Austrian university. This source finding does not supply raw data for computing new statistics. Broad-query result sets were not exhaustively paginated; exact-phrase, distinctive-word, DOI, and surname searches are recorded separately. Searches with identical URL/query repeated for output inspection are consolidated.
